subject: Physics
subtopic: Production, propagation, wave quantities and reflection
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

must_contain: Three distinct sound-production examples identifying the vibrating element: a stretched string, a stretched membrane, and an air column.
A vibrating source distinguished from the surrounding material medium.
A vacuum boundary showing that source vibration and sound propagation are different claims.

controlled_variation.vary: the sound-producing system from stretched string to stretched membrane to vibrating air column
controlled_variation.hold: the requirement that some physical source vibrates
controlled_variation.notice: the vibrating element changes, but vibration remains the common sound-production mechanism

controlled_variation.vary: the material medium from gas to liquid to solid
controlled_variation.notice: ordinary sound can propagate through different material media

controlled_variation.vary: the amount of material medium toward vacuum
controlled_variation.notice: ordinary sound propagation weakens as the mechanical transmission path is removed

must_contain: Compressions and rarefactions moving along one propagation axis.
One marked particle oscillating locally while the disturbance travels much farther.

controlled_variation.vary: the position of the compression pattern
controlled_variation.notice: the pattern propagates while the particle oscillates locally

controlled_variation.vary: particle displacement from forward to backward
controlled_variation.notice: longitudinal particle motion is parallel to the propagation axis

must_contain: A spatial sound-wave graph whose horizontal repeat distance is identified as wavelength.
A temporal sound-wave graph whose horizontal repeat time is identified as period.
Amplitude read from vertical extent without confusing it with wavelength or period.
An explicit derivation v = lambda/T = f lambda for one wave in one medium.

controlled_variation.vary: the horizontal graph coordinate from position to time
controlled_variation.notice: repeat spacing changes meaning from wavelength lambda to period T

controlled_variation.hold: the same wavelength and medium model

controlled_variation.notice: disturbance size can change without changing repeat spacing

engineering_dependencies.reason: Grade 9 frequency-period conversion needs gate ownership.
Grade 9 sound speed, frequency and wavelength relation needs gate ownership.
Period-to-frequency exits need the implemented Physics validator.
Wave-speed exits need the implemented Physics validator.
The Grade 9 curriculum explicitly requires graphical representation and analysis of sound waves.

must_contain: A matched-amplitude frequency comparison for pitch.
A matched-frequency sound-strength comparison for loudness.
The approximate usual human audible band stated as about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, with an explicit warning that individual limits vary.

controlled_variation.notice: higher frequency corresponds to higher pitch
loudness can change while pitch stays the same

controlled_variation.vary: frequency from below 20 Hz through 1,000 Hz to above 20,000 Hz
controlled_variation.notice: the examples move from below the usual audible band to within it and then above it

must_contain: An outward-and-return reflected path before echo distance is calculated.
A distinction between a separate echo and overlapping reverberation.
An echolocation example using return timing as a range cue.

controlled_variation.hold: sound speed in the same medium
controlled_variation.notice: round-trip echo delay changes in direct proportion
a distinct delayed return can be heard as echo while dense returns merge into reverberation

engineering_dependencies.reason: One-way range from round-trip echo timing needs gate ownership.
Numerical echo-range exits need the implemented Physics validator.

must_contain: Gol Gumbaz named only as the curriculum's historical reflected-sound/echo context, without an invented architectural-acoustics mechanism.
At least two Raman Research Institute-supported acoustics themes such as bowed/struck strings, resonance/maintenance of vibrations, or mridangam/tabla acoustics.
An explicit separation between Raman's acoustics work relevant to this Sound context and the higher-grade optical Raman effect.

controlled_variation.vary: the context from Gol Gumbaz to a generic wall echo
controlled_variation.notice: the historical example reuses reflection/echo ideas rather than introducing a new equation

controlled_variation.vary: the Raman acoustics example from strings to resonance to Indian musical drums
controlled_variation.notice: multiple documented research themes connect Raman to sound and musical instruments

family.invariant_demand: Identify source and medium, keep particle motion separate from wave propagation, distinguish the wave quantities, and trace reflection paths before calculating.
family.difficult_move: Knowing which quantity the words describe—particle displacement, amplitude, period, frequency, wavelength, wave speed, pitch, loudness or round-trip delay—before selecting a relation.
family.independent_check: Units and boundary cases must agree: fT=1, v=f lambda for one wave, and echo one-way range is half the round-trip path.

support_ladder.handed_over: Source, medium, axes and the target quantity are labelled.
Source/medium or the reflection path is labelled.
Only the real-world sound description is supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A compression/rarefaction description must be translated into local particle motion and propagation direction without drawing particles travelling with the wave.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which motion belongs to particles and which belongs to the disturbance

transfer.changed_demand: Frequency, amplitude and wavelength are all changed in a comparison, requiring separate pitch, loudness and speed reasoning rather than one 'bigger wave' judgment.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which physical quantity controls each percept/propagation relation

transfer.changed_demand: A cave-mapping or animal echolocation problem must be recognized as an ordinary reflected-sound round-trip timing problem.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that the measured delay contains both outward and return paths

transfer.changed_demand: A sampled sound graph must be identified as spatial or temporal before the learner can decide whether horizontal repeat spacing means wavelength or period.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the horizontal axis is position or time

transfer.changed_demand: A frequency just outside the approximate human audible band must be classified using the Grade 9 hearing-range model without treating 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz as exact personal hearing thresholds.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that the quoted audible band is an approximate usual human-hearing model rather than a universal biological cutoff

transfer.changed_demand: A historical/scientific context names Gol Gumbaz or C. V. Raman without handing over which already-taught Sound ideas are relevant.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that Gol Gumbaz is being used as a reflected-sound/echo context and that Raman had documented acoustics research distinct from the optical Raman effect
